prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Feel the patient’s heart Pounding—oh please, this once— —JAMES MERRILL I’ll do what I must if I’m bold in real time. A refugee, I’ll be paroled in real time. Cool evidence clawed off like shirts of hell-fire? A former existence untold in real time ... The one you would choose: Were you led then by him? What longing, O Yaar, is controlled in real time? Each syllable sucked under waves of our earth— The funeral love comes to hold in real time! They left him alive so that he could be lonely— The god of small things is not consoled in real time. Please afterwards empty my pockets of keys— It’s hell in the city of gold in real time. God’s angels again are—for Satan!—forlorn. Salvation was bought but sin sold in real time. And who is the terrorist, who the victim? We’ll know if the country is polled in real time. “Behind a door marked DANGER” are being unwound the prayers my friend had enscrolled in real time. The throat of the rearview and sliding down it the Street of Farewell’s now unrolled in real time. I heard the incessant dissolving of silk— I felt my heart growing so old in real time. Her heart must be ash where her body lies burned. What hope lets your hands rake the cold in real time? Now Friend, the Belovèd has stolen your words— Read slowly: The plot will unfold in real time. (for Daniel Hall)

prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Feel, Pounding, JAMES

outputs.L1:
*Feel the patient’s heart*  
*Pounding—oh please, this once—*  
—JAMES MERRILL  

I’ll do what I must if I’m bold in real time.  
A refugee, I’ll be paroled in real time.  

Cool evidence clawed off like shirts of hell-fire?  
A former existence untold in real time ...  

The one you would choose: Were you led then by him?  
What longing, O Yaar, is controlled in real time?  

Each syllable sucked under waves of our earth—  
The funeral love comes to hold in real time!  

They left him alive so that he could be lonely—  
The god of small things is not consoled in real time.  

Please afterwards empty my pockets of keys—  
It’s hell in the city of gold in real time.  

God’s angels again are—for Satan!—forlorn.  
Salvation was bought but sin sold in real time.  

And who is the terrorist, who the victim?  
We’ll know if the country is polled in real time.  

“Behind a door marked DANGER” are being unwound  
the prayers my friend had enscrolled in real time.  

The throat of the rearview and sliding down it  
the Street of Farewell’s now unrolled in real time.  

I heard the incessant dissolving of silk—  
I felt my heart growing so old in real time.  

Her heart must be ash where her body lies burned.  
What hope lets your hands rake the cold in real time?  

Now Friend, the Belovèd has stolen your words—  
Read slowly: The plot will unfold in real time.  

*(for Daniel Hall)*
outputs.L2:
Sense the sick man’s heart hammering—  
just grant me this single time—  
—JAMES MERRILL

I will carry out what is required,  
if I can be courageous in the present moment.  
As one displaced from home,  
I will be released under watch in the present moment.

Cold proof has been torn away  
like garments burning with infernal flame;  
some earlier life remains unspoken  
in the present moment.

Was he the one you would have selected?  
Were you guided by him back then?  
What desire, O Yaar,  
can be restrained in the present moment?

Every sound is pulled beneath  
the surges of our world;  
mourning love arrives  
to take possession in the present moment.

They spared his life  
only to leave him isolated;  
the deity of tiny matters  
finds no comfort in the present moment.

When it is over,  
please remove the keys from my pockets;  
the golden city  
is torment in the present moment.

Once more, the angels of God  
are desolate—for Satan’s sake.  
Redemption was purchased,  
yet wrongdoing was traded in the present moment.

Who is the one who terrorizes,  
and who is the one harmed?  
If the nation is surveyed,  
we will learn this in the present moment.

Beyond a door labeled DANGER,  
the prayers my friend had written out  
are being loosened and undone  
in the present moment.

The rearview mirror becomes a throat,  
and slipping down through it,  
the Street of Farewell  
spreads open in the present moment.

I heard silk  
continually coming apart;  
I felt my own heart  
becoming ancient in the present moment.

Her heart must be cinders  
where her burned body rests.  
What kind of hope lets your fingers  
scrape through the cold in the present moment?

Now, my Friend,  
the Beloved has taken your language from you.  
Read with care:  
the story will reveal itself in the present moment.

(for Daniel Hall)
outputs.L3:
The poem presents a speaker who confronts suffering not as an abstract idea, but as an urgent reality unfolding in the present moment. Exile, fear, and the demand for courage shape the emotional landscape of the poem. The speaker seems caught between endurance and action, aware that to live “now” requires a difficult form of bravery. This courage is not heroic in a simple or triumphant sense; rather, it is burdened by uncertainty, grief, and the knowledge that every choice takes place within a world already marked by violence and loss.

Throughout the poem, questions of identity, blame, and moral certainty remain unresolved. The speaker repeatedly circles around difficult categories such as terrorism, victimhood, sin, and salvation, refusing to treat them as simple or stable. Who is guilty, who is innocent, who suffers, and who is redeemed are not presented as easy questions. Instead, the poem exposes the instability of moral judgment in a world shaped by political conflict and spiritual anxiety. By doing so, it challenges any comfortable division between perpetrator and victim, righteousness and sin, despair and salvation.

The poem’s images of death, loneliness, and mourning deepen this sense of unresolved suffering. Grief is shown as continuous rather than temporary, something that does not end neatly or submit to consolation. The speaker’s sorrow appears to unfold moment by moment, suggesting that mourning is not a single event but an ongoing condition. Death is not only remembered; it remains present, haunting the speaker’s thoughts and shaping the atmosphere of the poem. Loneliness intensifies this grief, making the speaker’s pain feel both deeply personal and impossible to escape.

At the same time, the poem connects private heartbreak to broader political and spiritual crises. Personal loss is not isolated from public violence; instead, the two mirror and intensify one another. The speaker’s intimate suffering becomes inseparable from questions of war, terror, displacement, guilt, and faith. This fusion of the personal and the political gives the poem much of its force, as it suggests that heartbreak itself can be historical, and that public catastrophe enters the most private regions of feeling.

The repeated phrase “in real time” reinforces the poem’s immediacy. It makes the experience of loss, memory, and revelation feel as though it is occurring directly before the reader’s eyes. Rather than looking back from a safe distance, the poem seems to unfold in the very moment of crisis. This phrase also suggests that grief and understanding are not completed after the fact; they happen as life continues, without pause or resolution. In this way, the poem captures the rawness of experience as it is lived, emphasizing that suffering, memory, and moral reckoning are all taking place “in real time.”
outputs.L4:
The poem explores exile, terror, grief, and moral uncertainty through a ghazal-like sequence shaped by repetition, fragmentation, and direct address. Its recurring refrain, “in real time,” gives the poem a feeling of immediacy, as if violence and mourning are not distant historical events but experiences unfolding before the speaker and reader at the same moment. This repeated phrase also suggests the pressure of witnessing: suffering is not remembered calmly after the fact, but encountered as it happens, without the comfort of distance or resolution.

The poem’s fragmented images create a world marked by displacement and fear. Rather than presenting a single, linear narrative, it moves through flashes of memory, accusation, loss, and questioning. This broken structure mirrors the emotional and political conditions it describes: exile disrupts identity, terror interrupts ordinary life, and grief resists neat explanation. The poem’s direct questions intensify this uncertainty, forcing the reader to confront difficult moral problems rather than offering easy answers.

At the center of the poem is the sense that suffering collapses familiar distinctions. The boundaries between victim and perpetrator, past and present, private mourning and public violence become unstable. Memory does not remain safely in the past; it returns urgently, shaping the present moment. Likewise, grief is not only personal but political, tied to histories of injustice, displacement, and collective trauma.

By refusing closure, the poem makes grief feel immediate, unresolved, and morally demanding. Its repetitions do not soothe; instead, they insist that the reader remain aware of pain as something ongoing. In this way, the poem becomes both an elegy and a form of witness, asking how one can mourn, remember, and respond ethically in a world where violence continues “in real time.”

James could feel his heart pounding as he stood at the edge of the stage. The lights were bright, the room was silent, and every eye seemed to be waiting for him to speak. For a moment, doubt crept in, but he took a deep breath and reminded himself why he was there.

This was his chance — a moment he had worked toward for years. The pounding in his chest was no longer fear; it became energy, courage, and determination. James stepped forward, lifted his head, and began.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a ghazal in the style of Agha Shahid Ali, with the refrain “in real time,” an epigraph from James Merrill, political grief, exile, longing, and a dedication to Daniel Hall.
counterfactuals.output:
**For Daniel Hall**

*“Art. It cures affliction.”*  
—James Merrill, “Farewell Performance”

The border learned our names, then misspelled them in real time;  
a mother’s prayer became a siren’s hymn in real time.

On screens, the city burns; the anchor calls it weather.  
Ash falls from the mouth of every regime in real time.

Exile: that country where your key still turns in dreaming,  
where doors unlock to rooms you cannot claim in real time.

I carried home in a suitcase lined with winter.  
Customs found my grief and stamped it “seen” in real time.

Beloved, your window’s lit across an ocean of curfews;  
my longing keeps arriving, ship by ship, in real time.

The dead vote with their silence; the living count the ballots.  
Who audits all the blood beneath the crime in real time?

In Kashmir, in Gaza, in each broken alphabet of thunder,  
snow and dust translate the same old scream in real time.

Daniel, the poem is late; forgive its trembling postage.  
Even the heart must cross a checkpoint’s beam in real time.

Shahid is gone—yet listen: a veil of rain says “Stay.”  
I answer from my exile, line by line, in real time.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a contemporary English ghazal where every couplet ends with “in real time,” includes the word “Yaar,” references terrorism, refugees, angels, keys, and a “city of gold,” and closes with a self-addressing signature couplet.
counterfactuals.output:
At midnight, terror blooms across the headline in real time,  
and prayer becomes a trembling dotted line in real time,

Refugees carry homes in sacks, their children’s shoes untied,  
while borders refresh like apps that won’t align in real time,

Yaar, who can sleep when drones rehearse above the darkened roofs,  
and sirens translate fear into a sign in real time,

Angels, if you’re listening, come down from your cloud backups;  
we need your wings, not icons that just shine in real time,

A guard holds up the keys and says the shelter’s full tonight;  
the locks learn every human being’s design in real time,

Somewhere they promised us a radiant city of gold,  
but markets auction off its last skyline in real time,

Love texts a single heart, then vanishes beneath bad news;  
still, grief keeps typing: I am yours, be mine in real time,

O poet, call yourself by name before the signal dies—  
Yaar, sign your burning silence into line in real time,
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a poem modeled on Agha Shahid Ali’s “In Real Time,” preserving its formal ghazal structure, elegiac tone, and repeated refrain, but make it feel like an original literary homage.
counterfactuals.output:
I can’t reproduce Ali’s poem or closely echo its exact language, but here is an original ghazal-style homage, using an elegiac refrain and the traditional couplet structure.

**In Real Time**

The snow kept falling through the news, through each closed shrine, in real time.  
A voice crossed static, then became a broken line in real time.  

We learned the names of cities by the smoke above their gates;  
the map unfolded like a wound no hand could sign in real time.  

Your letters, once delayed by oceans, reached me all at once—  
ink turning back to breath, salt turning into wine in real time.  

What is a border but a bell rung under buried glass?  
What is exile but the hour refusing to decline in real time?  

I lit a candle; wind arrived as if it knew your room.  
The flame bowed once, then stood, a stubborn little spine in real time.  

The dead do not depart; they gather in the minor key,  
wearing our coats, correcting every borrowed line in real time.  

Somewhere a mother folds the dark into her child’s sleeve;  
somewhere a prayer is torn from its design in real time.  

Beloved, if grief is music, then we are its instruments—  
each rib a string, each silence tuned too fine in real time.  

Tonight the moon is thin as paper held against a lamp;  
I read your absence there, its watermark divine, in real time.  

And I, who sign this empty page with ash instead of name,  
keep waiting for your hand to finish mine in real time.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a lyrical poem with an epigraph “Feel the patient’s heart / Pounding—oh please, this once— —JAMES MERRILL,” ending each couplet with “in real time,” and dedicate it “for Daniel Hall.”
counterfactuals.output:
for Daniel Hall

“Feel the patient’s heart / Pounding—oh please, this once—”  
—JAMES MERRILL

The rain rehearses silver on the sill,  
and every drop arrives in real time,

as if the world, still learning how to grieve,  
kept taking down our pulse in real time,

as if the room were listening with its walls,  
each shadow leaning close in real time,

while somewhere bells unfasten from the air  
and scatter into light in real time.

I hold the fragile weather of a hand,  
its small, astonished warmth in real time,

and hear beneath the skin’s translucent hush  
the dark sea keeping faith in real time.

O heart, red metronome, unhidden flame,  
go on, go on, be brave in real time,

for love is not the afterword of loss  
but breath beside the bed in real time.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
